mechanism_narrative: A strong growth in GDP, as measured by GDPC1, indicates a robust demand environment that drives corporate earnings and subsequently leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 20d returns in > 40% of instances despite strong GDP growth, or the correlation between GDPC1 and SPX returns is not significant (p > 0.1) over the evaluation period.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate exceeds 4.5%, it signals a tightening monetary environment that increases borrowing costs for corporations, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 5d returns in > 50% of instances when FEDFUNDS is above 4.5%, or the average return during such periods is not significantly lower than the overall mean return (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: An increase in the unemployment rate, as measured by UNRATE, indicates a weakening labor market that negatively impacts consumer spending and subsequently leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20d returns in > 40% of instances despite rising unemployment, or the correlation between UNRATE and SPX returns is not significant (p > 0.1) over the evaluation period.

mechanism_narrative: When industrial production, as measured by INDPRO, grows at a rate exceeding 5% year-over-year, it signals a strong supply environment that supports economic growth and leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 60d returns in > 30% of instances when INDPRO growth is above 5%, or the average return during such periods is not significantly higher than the overall mean return (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: The interaction between strong housing market activity, as measured by HOUST, and low unemployment, as measured by UNRATE, indicates a robust demand environment that drives corporate earnings and subsequently leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 20d returns in > 40% of instances despite strong housing market and low unemployment, or the correlation between the interaction term of HOUST and UNRATE and SPX returns is not significant (p > 0.1) over the evaluation period.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate is below 2% and the consumer price index, as measured by CPIAUCSL, is rising at a rate exceeding 3% year-over-year, it signals an inflationary environment that erodes the purchasing power of consumers, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 5d returns in > 50% of instances when FEDFUNDS is below 2% and CPIAUCSL growth is above 3%, or the average return during such periods is not significantly lower than the overall mean return (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A decline in payroll employment, as measured by PAYEMS, indicates a weakening labor market that negatively impacts consumer spending and subsequently leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days, but only during periods of monetary easing.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20d returns in > 40% of instances despite declining payroll employment during easing periods, or the correlation between PAYEMS and SPX returns is not significant (p > 0.1) over the evaluation period.

mechanism_narrative: The interaction between strong industrial production growth, as measured by INDPRO, and rising housing market activity, as measured by HOUST, indicates a robust supply environment that supports economic growth and leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days, but only during periods of low inflation.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 60d returns in > 30% of instances despite strong industrial production growth and rising housing market activity during low-inflation periods, or the correlation between the interaction term of INDPRO and HOUST and SPX returns is not significant (p > 0.1) over the evaluation period.
